description: Application staging, environment configuration and asynchronous deployment lifecycle.

notes.text: Available from cPanel 138.

Names, paths, categories, modes and source values are forwarded unchanged and encoded once. Omission preserves upstream defaults; explicit empty strings and false/zero stay supplied. The client does not look up applications, upload/read source files, fetch returned URLs, poll, retry, merge configuration, restore or roll back. No universal live compatibility is established; attributed observations are limited to their stated original revision, server build, operations and routes.

Only supplied options change, but env and env_text replace ALL environment variables. Read the current set separately and submit the complete intended set. Pass one or the other; the server rejects their combination. Neither configure method reads or merges.

An empty environment object (raw {} or structured []), or env_text yielding no variables, clears the environment; clearing is allowed despite env_not_editable. Setting variables requires .env to be untracked and ignored by a committed .gitignore rule.

Server environment restrictions: JSON at most 16 KiB, at most 64 variables, names matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* and at most 128 characters, and single values at most 4096 characters without control characters. PORT is reserved. The client does not newly enforce these restrictions or promise universal upstream conversion of JSON scalar null; the attributed build-specific behavior is described below.

env_text splits at the first =; later duplicate names win. Quotes and spaces remain literal without quote stripping; a noncomment line without = is rejected by the server. The client forwards the text unchanged.

appdir is relative to the source root; empty resets it. A change reruns preflight and suggested defaults, with explicitly supplied values taking precedence. Empty build/startup commands clear their overrides; nonstatic applications lacking both commands cannot deploy.

An empty domain regenerates the default. useExistingDomain=true confirms takeover and hides the existing website; omission does not confirm, and false cannot revoke prior confirmation. Changing the domain releases the prior include. A domain owned by another application is still rejected.

The optional deployed, env_editable and staged response fields return integer 0|1. Native JSON integer flags were reported on cPanel 11.138.0.19 through direct UAPI and WHM bridge for this operation at original revision 4ab5b80587f8d524bbc0ccf5129f9901ef9ab8df. Pinned formal booleans remain accepted as source compatibility and normalize to 0|1; booleans are not an observed wire claim. Strings, other integers, floats and null remain invalid. This does not establish deployment or running-container compatibility.

On cPanel 11.138.0.19, seebeen reported on both direct UAPI and WHM bridge at original revision 4ab5b80587f8d524bbc0ccf5129f9901ef9ab8df that the server stores environment values as TEXT: number 5 becomes "5", float 1.5 becomes "1.5", true becomes "1", false becomes "0", and null becomes "". The nonempty string "0" can be truthy in application code. This is server conversion: configureStructured still serializes the original native JSON types and bytes in one form field without client text conversion. Its parameter description that scalar null stays JSON null describes client encoding. Each supplied environment replaces the full set; structured [] emits {} and clears it, while null for the whole optional input omits the field. These are attributed version-scoped observations, not a universal conversion or persistence guarantee.

Registers source only; configure optionally, then deploy separately. ZIP/tar source paths refer to previously uploaded archives relative to the account home; Git sources are URLs. The client never uploads, reads or fetches the source. Only use trusted sources: the server builds and executes them.

Never embed credentials in a Git URL: upstream stores it in plaintext. Prefer the account SSH key option. A staged-name collision overwrites its source; a deployed-name collision assigns the next free name-N. Use the returned name and domain for subsequent calls.

Default source-root detection, default Git branch and runtime are left upstream. parent must be owned exactly, not merely its parent; omission/empty uses the main domain. sshKeyName applies only to git@ sources. Only modern encrypted OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY keys can be unlocked; legacy encrypted PEM keys are rejected upstream.
sshKeyPass is sent only as sshkeypass in the selected POST form body; omitted passphrases stay omitted. The client never prompts for or stores them.
